title: Preparing a Queensland home for sale
description: Things to prepare before listing a Queensland home: smoke alarms, the pool, owner-builder work and, if it is rented, the tenant. Summarised from QBCC, Queensland Fire Department and RTA pages.

sources.title: Buy, sell or lease a property with a pool
When a property is for sale

items.title: Check every smoke alarm is photoelectric, interconnected and hardwired or 10-year battery powered
items.detail: AS 3786-2014, no ionisation sensor, less than 10 years old and working when tested.

items.title: Check there is an alarm in every bedroom, in hallways connecting bedrooms and on every storey
Find the current pool safety certificate, or book a licensed pool safety inspector
If there will be no certificate, prepare the Form 36 notice for the QBCC and the buyer
If owner-builder work was finished in the last 6 years, prepare two copies of the owner-builder notice
If the home is rented, give the tenant a Notice of lessor's intention to sell (Form 10)
Give an Entry notice (Form 9) before each showing, and get the tenant's written agreement for open houses or an on-site auction
Ask the tenant before photographing the home for advertising
Plan around the tenancy: a fixed term continues after the sale, and a periodic tenancy needs at least 2 months' notice to leave after contracts are signed
At settlement, have the tenant told about the new owner and update the RTA's bond record (Form 5)
